text: Refines D-0323 and D-0324 for #555: a run push's permission check never starves behind lease renewal. Renewals and the release run one at a time under a lock of their own, held through their git read and push. The lock on the lease's state, its expiry, tenure and pushes, is never held across a git call: a renewal takes it only to read that state before its push and to record the outcome after. A run push takes the clone's lock, then checks its permission, so nothing that holds the lease state waits for the clone. A step's check during a renewal's git sees the lease last confirmed. With the lease's and run records' git commands 50 ms slower, #463's drain test passes in all four subtests, where it failed in all four before.
